messages.subject: Mice Example from WinBUGS
parts:
I am about to submit revisions on a paper, and after reading through my methods section again (after a long while of not working on this project), I realized (to my horror) that I no longer really understand a critical line in my model code. This issue comes from the Stan version of the WinBUGS Mice model. The model lines are pasted below. I understand what is going on in the first 'for' loop (this is the observed age of death loop), but the second loop I don't understand very well. t2_censored is a missing data parameter, and censor_time is the observed age of censoring, but why do we divide the second argument of the Weibull by the time of censoring? Should t2_censored be understood as an estimated age of death, or estimated time lived passed the censoring threshold?

My intuition is that this goes back to an old thread about allowing for variable 'time of censoring' constraints in the model, but I'm not quite sure of how this creates such behavior.

model {
  r ~ exponential(0.001);
  beta ~ normal(0, 100);
  for (n in 1:N_uncensored) {
    t_uncensored[n] ~ weibull(r, exp(-beta[group_uncensored[n]] / r));
                            }
    for (n in 1:N_censored) {
    t2_censored[n] ~ weibull(r, exp(-beta[group_censored[n]] / r) / censor_time[n]);
                          }
}

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Mice Example from WinBUGS
parts:
If we were able to specify a vector lower bound in stan, we would have

 t_censored[n] ~ weibull(r, exp(-beta[group_censored[n]] / r));

where t_censored are parameters and are defined as

real<lower=censor_time> t_censored.

But we cannot do the above, so a t2_censored is defined with lower bound 1.  Essentially,
t2_censored = t_censored / censor_time


Then the distribution of t2_censored needs to be derived from the distribution of t_censored and that is why the second argument of the weibull distribution is divided by censor_time.


Jiqiang

From Jiqiang:
---------------

If we were able to specify a vector lower bound in stan, we would have

t_censored[n] ~ weibull(r, exp(-beta[group_censored[n]] / r));

where t_censored are parameters and are defined as

real<lower=censor_time> t_censored.

But we cannot do the above, so a t2_censored is defined with lower bound 1. Essentially,
t2_censored = t_censored / censor_time

Then the distribution of t2_censored needs to be derived from the distribution of t_censored and that is why the second argument of the weibull distribution is divided by censor_time.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Mice Example from WinBUGS
parts: Exactly. We usually model lambda=exp(XB) but this lambda is not the scale sigma of the Weibull. In fact, lambda=1/(sigma^shape). Hence we have sigma of stan as sigma= exp(_XB/shape).
